Before this: 'does this holder have this remit act' had THREE readings over TWO stores -- `loop/resolve.py`'s `_eligible` and `epistemic.py`'s `_ch_post_remit` both read the live `w.offices[x].remit_acts`, while `decision/options.py` already read the Tenure-side snapshot, `Tenure.granted_acts` -- a duplication `CLAUDE.md` §8 forbids that three independent read-only review lanes rediscovered separately before this fix. BUILT: both world-side readers now admit on `t.granted_acts`, deleting the `w.offices.get` read each one carried; `decision/options.py`'s own reading needed no change. VERIFIED BY AN ANTAGONIST PASS (independent, no access to the builder's reasoning) THAT CAUGHT A REAL REGRESSION BEFORE THIS LANDED: an existing test, `test_the_revocation_branch_executes_in_the_fold_and_not_only_as_a_predicate` (`test_season_shape.py`), hand-mutated `off_duke.remit_acts` AFTER `tiny_world()` had already seated the actor on it -- exactly the read/write asymmetry (`CLAUDE.md` §0.1 pt 1) this position exists to close, and it had worked only because the pre-fix resolver still read the live office. The builder's own whole-tree grep for a fourth reader deliberately excluded `tests/`, so it could not have seen this. Reproduced directly (the test failed exactly as the critic predicted) and fixed by seating the actor on a second office whose remit already carries the act at construction (`_seat`'s own default), rather than by mutating an office after the fact. A second, smaller gap was closed rather than left: `_ch_post_remit`'s half of the fix had no behavioural test anywhere in the tree -- its one existing caller-side test exercises an office whose remit never changes after seating, so it passes identically whether the channel reads the snapshot or the live office. A new test builds the actual disagreement (a holder whose office gains a remit act only live, never in the snapshot, witnessing a real emitted Event) and was verified to redden against the pre-fix reading before being accepted. Three docstrings this position's own change made false in the present tense -- `state/world.py::_grant_remit`'s claim that '`_eligible` ... reads `w.offices` directly', and two passages inside `test_h71_the_grant_is_a_snapshot_not_a_mirror` describing the same since-closed gap as current -- corrected with dated notes, the original reasoning kept as history rather than deleted. Two board rows in `plan.md` (`13e` and `13f`) that still read `OPEN` though `13f` had already landed two commits ago -- a defect CLAUDE.md §0.2 names directly -- are flipped to `DONE` in the same commit. FINAL STATE: `engine/season/tests -q -n auto` 293 passed (290 after `13f` plus 3 this position's own tests: the two-arm resolver falsifier, the AST scan, and the new witness-channel test); the two `tests/valoria` files most exposed to this diff both pass; `runs/TRACE.txt`/`runs/results.json` regenerated with zero diff, confirming the fix is behaviourally neutral on every world the corpus and probes currently build (every builder seats holders after constructing their offices, so snapshot and live office never disagreed there -- the disagreement this position protects against is reachable only through a hand-mutation, which is exactly what the caught regression was).
